summary: Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University (~1944–1983), where he became an emeritus professor.
Shunpaku Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Shuchiin University, where he is attested as an assistant professor in 1963 and as a professor in 1976.

Shunryu Suzuki (1904–1971) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji, and with traditional teachers including Gyokujun So-on and Ian Kishizawa. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Sōkō-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center.

Shunsho Manabe (1939–2021) worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. After studying at Tohoku University (~1960–1964), he held positions at Hosen Gakuen College (~1986–1997) and as a professor at Shikoku University (~2005–2017).
Shunsho Terakawa (1928–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1953). He served at Otani University (~1967–2000), where he became an emeritus professor.
Shuntaro Kondo (b. 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Ryukoku University by 2011 and served there as a part-time lecturer in 2012.

Shuntaro Matsuyama (1930–2014) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, and held teaching posts at Bigakko, Tama Art University, Kokugakuin University, and Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1973–1996).

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning a D.Lit. from Bukkyo University by 1993, he served there as an associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka (1927–2009) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University (doctorate, 1962). He served as an assistant professor at Toyo University (~1966–1992).
Shuyu Sakurai (b. 1916) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1940–1943). He later held a post at Komazawa University (~1962–1987), where he became an emeritus professor.

Shwe Zan Aung (1871–1932) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. at the University of Rangoon (~1888–1891) and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.
Shōkō Kabutogi (1912–1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University (~1933–1936) and later served there as a professor (~1963–1983).

Shōren Ihara (1923–1999) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at Kyushu University as an assistant professor (attested 1959–1965, 1977) and was a member at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

Shōyū Hanayama (1931–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1960). He served as vice president at Musashino University (~1968–1995) and chairperson at Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai until 1995.

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014). He also studied under multiple traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala and U Sajjanasāra.

Sibani Das Gupta is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Dhaka and completed a doctorate at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under Sushil Kumar De, having also studied under Rajendra Chandra Hazra.

Sibaraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma and several other teachers. He served as a Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).

Sibnath Sarma is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He worked at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir and served as a professor of philosophy at Gauhati University (attested 1999–2012).
Sibylle Koch is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at the University of Oxford and earned a master's degree at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2012–2015).

Sicheng Liang (1901–1972) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Beijing Huiwen Middle School, Tsinghua University (~1915–1923), and the University of Pennsylvania School of Design (~1924–1927). He held a post at Peking University (~1946–1952).
